claims.text: Tailored thermo-mechanical processing can induce a refined duplex lamellar microstructure in eutectic high-entropy alloys.
Increasing local Cr content promotes micro-phase separation and formation of the targeted hierarchical duplex lamellar structure.
Optimized casting followed by controlled rolling and annealing will create the targeted duplex lamellar structure.
Standard-cast or conventionally processed HEAs have a relatively homogeneous microstructure and lower Cr content.
The proposed structure consists of nanoscale Cr-rich or stabilizing phases interleaved with a softer matrix.
Hierarchical structural heterogeneity produces a two-hierarchical constraint effect during deformation.
The duplex lamellar architecture provides in situ composite behavior.
The hierarchical lamellar structure generates a microcrack-arresting mechanism.
Higher Cr content increases resistance to localized deformation and improves the strength-ductility balance.
The duplex architecture improves load distribution and creates barriers to deformation and crack propagation.
The proposed microstructure increases work hardening and thereby delays localized necking and fracture.
Stable interfacial bonding in the lamellar alloy improves effective stiffness and toughness.
The intervention will simultaneously improve strength and ductility relative to conventionally processed or as-cast HEAs.
Yield strength will increase by approximately 10-20% relative to the control or state-of-the-art comparator.
Elongation at failure will increase by approximately 10-15%.
Young's modulus will increase by approximately 5-10%.
The intervention will improve fracture resistance.
The property improvements require Cr content, deformation, annealing temperature, and annealing time to lie within an optimal processing window.
The improvements may disappear when phase decomposition or the targeted duplex lamellar architecture is not produced.

contradictions.description: The baseline is described as having lower Cr and the intervention includes enhanced Cr content, but the proposed experiment says the treated and control samples have identical base compositions. It is therefore unclear whether Cr content is changed only in the treated group, held constant in both groups, or independently controlled.
